steps.action: Register provider with an issuer that cannot be reached
steps.actual: Register provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The change could not be saved. Try again." and no provider was stored.

steps.action: Register provider against the local OpenID Connect fixture; copy the callback URL; registration turns on nothing
steps.expected: Saved; callback ends /api/auth/sso/callback on the instance address; SSO switches stay off; Provider ID fixed
steps.actual: Register provider showed Saved and "Paste this callback URL into your IdP console: http://127.0.0.1:23310/api/auth/sso/callback". Both Single sign-on (SSO) switches stayed off but became available (["false","false"]). After reload the Provider ID field was gone and the button read Save provider.

steps.action: Turn on Single sign-on (SSO) under Legal User Authentication; an invited staff account signs in through the identity provider
steps.expected: Callback succeeds; role Legal team member retained; row becomes Active
steps.actual: The switch saved ("Saved"). In a separate browser, Continue with single sign-on went through the fixture's authorize endpoint and the OpenLaw callback to /, signed in as legal_team_member. The invited row now read Active with a role control (true).

steps.action: An uninvited identity on a matching email domain gets no staff role
steps.expected: No staff session; no staff account
steps.actual: With Business Portal single sign-on off, doc029-auth-uninvited-mu4ff2mk@helix.example (matching the provider's helix.example domain, not an allowed Portal domain) ended on /auth/login?error=sso with me 401 and "Single sign-on failed. Try again.". Account created: none.

steps.action: Save provider with Client secret left blank, then with a replacement secret; test a fresh sign-in after each
steps.expected: Saved both times; staff SSO still works
steps.actual: The Client secret hint read "Leave blank to keep the current secret. Paste a new value to rotate." Saving a Client ID change with a blank secret showed Saved; a fresh staff SSO sign-in worked (me 200). Saving a replacement secret showed Saved; another fresh sign-in worked (me 200). Stored client ID: doc029-client-mu4ff2mk.

steps.action: Update the issuer to one that cannot be reached
steps.expected: Refused; the previous provider stays usable
steps.actual: Save provider with an unreachable issuer showed "The change could not be saved. Try again.". The stored issuer stayed http://oidc:8080 and a fresh staff SSO sign-in still worked (me 200).

steps.action: Turn on Single sign-on (SSO) under Business Portal Authentication; an existing Business User signs in through the identity provider, and still can after the domain is removed
steps.expected: Existing Business User on the provider's email domain enters the Portal before and after narrowing the list; no staff role is granted
steps.actual: helix.example was added, and doc029-auth-bu-mu4ff2mk@helix.example entered the Portal through a sign-in link. The Business Portal SSO switch saved ("Saved"). Portal single sign-on for that existing Business User reached /portal/onboarding as business_user. After Remove helix.example (list now ["northwind.example"]), the same identity still signed in through single sign-on (/portal/onboarding, business_user). A never-seen identity on the removed domain ended on /portal/login?error=sso with "Single sign-on failed. Try again." and no account was created.

steps.action: Recover: Administrator password sign-in with Email and password off under Legal, then turn on Email and password and turn off SSO
steps.expected: Admin password sign-in works; staff login returns to password; SSO off
steps.actual: With only Single sign-on (SSO) on for Legal users ({"password":false,"magicLink":false,"sso":true,"requireTwoFactor":false}), the Administrator still signed in with a password (me 200). Turning Email and password and Email magic link back on and SSO off in both cards gave {"legal":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false},"business":{"password":true,"magicLink":true,"sso":false,"requireTwoFactor":false}}, and the Legal Team Member signed in with a password again (me 200).
